comment: Dr. Waddle is so nice and she ends class early half the time. Tests are hard but she has review sessions and will give you feedback on homeworks. She is a super timely grader, and responds to emails really fast. Take her for macro.

I'm sorry to be the odd one out here but I would nottt take her again. I had such an easy time in Micro and now in Macro I'm so lost. She lectures so fast and so randomly, it's impossible to digest. That being said, getting a good grade in this class isn't the hardest thing in the world but there are better econ professors here.

Dr. Waddle was the best! She is so nice and definitely cares a lot about her students. Weekly quizzes based on the optional homework that are super straightforward. She is very knowledgable about macro and applies the class to real world topics which I really appreciated. Her exams are difficult but it is definitely attainable to get an A.

Dr. Waddle is fantastic and so funny. Her lectures are great, and she uses handout packets. You do have quizzes every week and a group project, but they're pretty straightforward. Don't underestimate her exams; it's a good amount of analysis, but you can definitely get an A if you study enough. She has so much knowledge! Take her!
The actual GOAT. Be prepared for weekly quizzes, which are very similar to the homework. If you understand the content, the tests are not too hard. Overall, very nice and easy to understand.

She is so iconic. Graded on participation, but not a big deal. Tests are not too bad if you study the packets and given review materials. One group project about the stock market during the second half of the semester. Overall, great prof!!

Dr. Waddle is very passionate about economics. I really enjoyed her class because she didn't only focus on the content, we also talked a lot about what was going on in the real world and how that related to what we were learning. If you prepare for the tests, you should do well in the class.

Dr. Waddle is one of the most passionate econ professors I've had. She brings macro theory to life with real-world readings/podcasts/videos and even invited the ex-chair of the Richmond Fed! She's hilarious, super kind, and genuinely cares. Weekly-ish quizzes are just homework questions, and she's always happy to review them with you.

Her class was amazing! Gives you packets to take notes with in class so makes studying for exams very manageable. Super nice and understanding. Exams are straight forward nothing you didnt go over in class.

She's a QUEEEEEN. So nice. Her classes can be a little boring because every class is set up the exact same way, just by taking notes in a packet. But you do learn, and the quizzes/tests are so light. She's super caring, love her.
Best macro professor ever! Super understanding and sweet. Likes to engage with students and is helpful in office hours.

Content is rather technical, but Waddle more than makes up for it by communicating clearly and making the classes engaging. She cares about participation so definitely show up and raise your hand if she asks questions. Great teacher, great class. You get the opportunity to take a do-over exam if you mess up a test.

One of the best professors at UR. Clear with expectations, organized, and a good-sense of humor. Material and homework/quizzes are reasonable as they directly align with exams. Very reasonable person.

The hardest part was knowing how to tie the class concepts with real world situations. There's also a weekly quiz, but it's nothing crazy as long as you did the reading. Otherwise, Dr. Waddle is a funny and caring professor. She makes sure everyone is engaged in class discussion and jokes around very often.

Dr. Waddle is a caring educator and explains complicated concepts clearly. Homework (quizzes & short readings) is straightforward with one stock market project. The most difficult part of the course was the synthesis section of the exams which asks you to connect concepts together and clearly explain your reasoning for the solutions you identified.

Dr. Waddle is great. Her lectures can get a little confusing but with a bit of studying, her tests are fairly simply, which is where much of your grade comes from. There is a group project, but it isn't difficult. She can be a tough grader, but with normal participation and doing well on the weekly quizzes, the class should be pretty easy.

TAKE DR. WADDLE!!!! Dr. Waddle is the best. She is so understanding and listens to the needs of her students. Her lectures are really clear and dive deeper than just textbook economics. She is a challenging grader, but wants you to do well in the class.

Professor Waddle is a really good professor and helps you through complicated models that may seem really tough at first. The pace of the class was just right and her class has a good structure where content of the class builds off one another.

Professor Waddle is easily one of my favorite professors at the University of Richmond. She is very accessible outside of class and really wants to see her students succeed. Participation does matter but all the work in the class is very straightforward, and she always explains how to do problems before assigning them.
Solid overall teacher. She's nice and enthusiastic about teaching. Class is practically mandatory if you want a good grade, and she grades you on participation every single class.

Hard to get back on track if you miss something, participation is really important but there's limited time/space given for it, teaching is concise but doesn't match up with her test questions, honestly don't feel like I learned much from her class.

Dr. Waddle is a good professor. I honestly learned a lot about real-world econ and I even used that information to my poli sci papers. The sad thing is that her exam questions were very different from what we would do in class and a lot of the questions were about things she only mentioned once in class. You will learn a lot, but your GPA may drop

Professor Waddle is great, easily my favorite Econ professor. She loves Economics and really strives to make the material interesting. There is a good bit of work but its not crazy and she definitely wants you to succeed. 10/10 would recommend.
She is very average. Nice lady, clear about what will be on tests and what she is looking for while she is grading. I don't feel like I particularly learned a lot.
Dr Waddle is very approachable and makes it easy to be interested in the subject. Definitely not an easy class, but I learned a lot.

Dr. Waddle is very nice but has super high standards. She's a tough grader on test questions for sure, and if you mess up early on it is really difficult to get back on track. If you are good at being consistent with homework and teachers you will be ok but she is not easy.
Definitely one of the best in the bschool. Had her for principles and theory, would take her again in a heartbeat. She is super accessible in office hours, so be sure to take advantage of that.

Professor Waddle is super clear in her lectures and what you need to know. There are weekly articles to read and homework quizzes to complete. She gives ample opportunities to speak with her or a student assistant. She only tests you on things which were clearly covered in class. I was not good at 101 but excelled in her class!

Waddle is a very caring teacher if you go out of your way to get to know her.  There is a large group project that lasts the whole semester but you can pick your group partners.  Weekly homework quiz and two large exams throughout the semester.  Overall, a great teacher and I will be taking her again next year.

Dr. Waddle is super approachable, and if you make an effort to get to know her from the beginning it will pay off. Coming from an awful 101 experience, I thought the class was much more manageable and entertaining. Usually lets you out early too. Office hours are a must and studying for the homework quizzes really pays off. She gives great outlines

Prof Waddle is fun but knowledgable. The test questions sometimes come out of the blue, but if you go to reviews and office hours, you'll feel prepared for almost anything that she asks. Also, she's very approachable and nice in office hours.
Dr. Waddle is very helpful and hilarious. The course involved a lot of MATLAB and programming. It's challenging, but you will learn a lot.
Young blood
boring lectures, no class participation at all
